column4: I caught my husband cheating with a girl half his age.
She was twenty-six. He was fifty.
And the only reason I didn't break...
was what my sister flew in from Kerala to show me.
Came home early on a Thursday afternoon
Heard laughing up the stairs, there they were, in our room
I didn't scream, not yet, sat downstairs till the sky went black
Then the bathroom mirror finally stared back
Forty-seven, but I moved like seventy
Knees went at forty-four, then my back gave up on me
Held the railing every stair, couldn't sit down to pray
Watched my niece's mehendi from a plastic chair all day
Stopped wearing sarees, couldn't bend to pleat
Standing in that mirror, I knew why he'd cheat
Painkillers, sprays and balms, eight hundred every session
Doctor never looked up, "It's your age," that was his lesson
Forty-seven, moving like seventy
The mirror showed a woman I didn't want to be
He didn't even hide it, didn't even try
The pain took my body, then it took my pride
I called my sister Shalini, Kerala twenty years
I'm on the next flight, don't argue, she said through my tears
Got off the plane, no hug, hands on my shoulders, true
Kavita, you're not staying like this. We've got work to do.
Three days later, an amber bottle on the shelf
Those women dancing at sixty, they look after themselves
I said, "I need painkillers, not oil"
She said, "Pills just hide it, sprays sit on the skin
In Kerala we warm it in our palms and work it in
Ten minutes every night, four weeks, that's the deal
EIS Ayurvedic Pain Relief Oil, fifteen herbs in pure til
First night, the warmth went deep into my knee
Night three, I slept straight through, finally
Week one, no railing, week two, cross-legged to pray
My daughter called, "Mumma, you sound different today"
Week three, morning walks out on Carter Road
Week four, yoga, and I laughed out loud
Week six, the silk saree I never wore
Pleated it myself and cried on the bedroom floor
'Cause I finally felt like me
A friend brought Vikram, and the divorce came fast
Then a Bandra rooftop dinner, I looked up from my glass
My husband walked in, same girl on his arm
In the blue shirt I bought him for Diwali, all that charm
Halfway through dinner, he was staring, couldn't turn around
Mouth half open, like he'd seen a ghost in town
In the washroom, a woman, fifties, hand on her back
Sorry, I have to ask, you can't be forty, not like that
I told her 'bout the bottle, ten minutes every night
She ordered at the sink, cash on delivery, that night
I walked out, he was standing there alone
Kavita, you look... what did you do?
I didn't say a word, walked past him, back to my own
He didn't leave 'cause I got old, he couldn't handle a woman his age
Pain was never my age, now I've turned the page
Strong, awake, alive, forty-seven, and I choose
To be the woman he should've been terrified to lose

Fifty percent off, cash on delivery, thirty-day money-back guarantee.
Ten minutes a night. That's all it took for me.
